. The brief facts of the Prosecution case are as follows:
The accused No.1 since from the date of marriage with C.W.1 Smt.Netra was extending physical and mental cruelty towards her and on 16.11.2012 at about 8-30 am.

when CW1 came along with CW4 to attend the 11th day Death Ceremony of her father in law at No.66, 6th Cross, 6th Main, Pillappa Block, Ganganagar, the accused No.1 did not allow CW1 to participate in the Death Ceremony and the accused No.1 without any provocation assaulted CW1 and CW4 with hands and caused hurt and the accused No.1 criminally intimidated to the life of C.W.1 and thereby the accused No.1, 3 and 6 for the offences punishable U/S.498A, 323, 506 r/w 34 of IPC.

3. On the basis of the Statement of CW-1, the R.T. Nagara Police have registered a case under Crime No.420/2012 for the offences punishable U/S.498A, 324, 506 r/w 34 of IPC against the accused No.1 to 6 and submitted the FIR before the court.

Thereafter investigating officer visited the spot and drawn the spot mahazar and recorded the statement of witnesses on completion of the investigation, the Charge Sheet has been filed against the accused No. 1, 3 and 6 for the offence punishable U/S.498A, 323, 506 r/w 34 of IPC.
In the charge sheet the accused No.2, 4 and 5 are left out and the accused No.3 is reported to be dead.
In view of the death of accused No.3 case against accused No.3 is abated.
On the receipt of the police report, this court has taken cognizance for the said offences.
On the appearance of the accused No.1 and 6, the accused No.1 and 6 were released on bail.
Accused No.6 is discharged as per order dated 17-10-2018.
4. The copies of prosecution papers were furnished to the accused No.1 as contemplated U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.
After hearing both the parties, the charge was framed against the accused No.1 and read over to him.
Accused No.1 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Hence, the matter was posted for evidence.

5. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1 the prosecution has got examined 4 witnesses as PW-1 to 4, out of the total charge sheet witnesses as CW-1 to 10, and got marked four documents as Ex.P1 to P4 with sub markings.

During the course of cross examination of PW1 she got confronted and got marked document as Ex.D1 to D4.
6.
Learned A.P.P prayed for issuance of summons, NBW, Proclamation to CW2, 3, 5 and 6.
Inspite of giving sufficient opportunities to I.O. to execute summons, NBW, Proclamation the witnesses have not been secured.
Hence, the evidence of CW2, 3, 5 and 6 are dropped by rejecting the prayer of the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor.
Learned A.P.P. prays this court to given up the evidence of CW7 and 8.
In view of submission made by learned A.P.P. the evidence of CW7 and 8 is given up.
7. After closure of prosecution evidence, the accused No.1 is examined U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
Each and every incriminating circumstances found in the evidence of the prosecution against the accused No.1 is separately read over to the accused No.1.
The accused No.1 denied all such circumstances as false.

15. CW1-Smt.Netra examined as PW1 in her evidence deposed that on 23-02-2003 her marriage took place with accused No.1 at Bengaluru.
After marriage she went to matrimonial home.
Since 8 years she was residing separately since the accused No.1 having illicit relationship with one Rathna (accused No.2) and they are residing as husband and wife.
On 06/11/2012 her father in law died.
Accused No.1 did not inform about this incident.
On 07/11/2012 she came to know that her father in law died and cremation is going at Hebbal.
She went to Hebbal Burial ground.
She saw that the accused No.1 and 2 were performing rituals as if they are husband and wife.
She did not make galata under those circumstances.
On 08/11/2012 she went to the burial ground at Hebbal along with her children to attend further ritual ceremony.
The accused No.1 and 2 were performing pooja.
The accused No.1 scolded her objecting for her visit without invitation.
The accused No.1 did not allow her to put milk and ghee as a part of practice of ritual ceremony.
On 16/11/2012 she and her children went to the house of accused No.1 to attend death ceremony of her father in law.
The accused No.1 and 2 were performing pooja.
She raised objection for them to perform pooja and she also questioned their relation.
The accused No.1 objected for her visit without invitation abused her in filthy language and assaulted her.
She sustained injury on her hand.
The accused No.1 told her that she should die along with her children.
16. CW4/Gowramma examined as PW2 and deposed in her evidence that, CW.1 residing separately from her husband.
She cannot say since how many years she is residing separately.
In the year 2012 one day at about 11 a.m, she CW.1 and her children went to the house of accused No.1 to attend death ceremony of father of accused No.1.
The accused No.1 and 2 were performing pooja.

P.W.4 being an official witness has deposed regarding the investigation carried out by him and filing of charge sheet after completion of investigation.

The evidence of this witness is only regarding investigation done by him, but his evidence is not pointing to the offences alleged against accused No.1 or the involvement of the accused No.1 in the alleged crime.

20. PW1 is the daughter of PW2.

21. " As per Sec. 498A of the IPC.
"Sec.498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty-Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman,
subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term,
which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation: for the purpose of this section.

"
cruelty" means- (a) any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand".
22. By considering the evidence of P.W.1, 2 and by comparing the contents of evidence, complaint and statement before police, there is a contradictory statement with respect of harassment.
As I have already discussed the evidence which has been examined by the prosecution i.e., PW1 and 2 is of interested witnesses.

23. Further more on the issue of appreciation of evidence of interested witnesses, Dalip Singh Vs.
State of Punjab, AIR 1953 SC 364 -1954 SCR 145, is one of the earliest cases on the point.

In that case, it was held as follows:

"A witness is normally to be considered independent unless he or she springs from sources which are likely to be tainted and that usually means unless the witness has cause, such as enmity against the accused, to wish to implicate him falsely.
Ordinarily, a close relative would be the last to screen the real culprit and falsely implicate an innocent person.

It is true, when feelings run high and there is personal cause for enmity, that there is a tendency to drag in an innocent person against whom a witness has a grudge along with the guilty, but foundation must be laid for such a criticism and the mere fact of relationship far from being a foundation is often a sure guarantee of truth.
24.
Apart from the interested witnesses, no other eye witnesses, mahazar witnesses have been examined.
Further the prosecution has failed to prove the allegations made by the complainant.
Further there are no records before this court to prove the allegations made by the complainant against accused No.1 and his family.

25. Moreover it is pertinent to note that the accused No.1 has filed matrimonial case against the complainant which is numbered as M.C.No.1603/2021 on the file of VI Additional Family Court at Bengauru.
